title: VideoGenerationV1InputExample
description: Neutral public example for video.generate input: one operation with inputMode=first_last_frame, pixel width/height size representation, fixed fps, enum durationSeconds, ranged seed/width/height, optional negativePrompt, ordered media refs. Not a platform package and not a combination rule engine.

inputMode.description: One operation declares exactly one inputMode via const. Selecting another mode means selecting another operation with full identity.

prompt.description: User-confirmed full prompt text. Preserve newlines and any material-reference text; do not truncate or rewrite.

negativePrompt.description: Optional. Declare only when supported. Empty string means the user cleared the field; do not restore a default.

durationSeconds.description: Duration in whole seconds. This example uses enum. Alternatives: const (fixed) or minimum/maximum/multipleOf (range). Do not advertise fractional seconds as connected unless the consumer truly supports them.

fps.description: Generation frame rate in frames/second. This example uses a fixed const. Alternatives: enum or integer range. Submit the declared fixed value even when the control is locked; do not overwrite with playback fps.

aspectRatio.description: Aspect ratio strings come from the package declaration. Unusual declared values such as 9:5 must not be filtered by a local common-ratio whitelist. Matching aspect to width/height is adapter business validation.

width.description: Pixel width. This example uses the pixel size representation. Do not also send resolution or resolutionValue in the same request.

height.description: Pixel height. Same size-representation rule as width.

seed.description: Integer seed within the declared range. Hosts that use IEEE-754 numbers must stay within the exact integer range they can represent; out-of-range values are structural errors, not silent truncation.

firstFrame.description: Ordered first-frame image refs. Bytes travel on the existing controlled media channel; only mediaId appears here.

referenceAudios.description: Optional ordered reference audio refs. Usage is advanced.audioUsage; do not confuse reference audio with generate-audio output options.

advanced.description: Closed scalar set declared by the package. Host-side vendorFeatureDraft keys must land only on declared advanced (or other declared) fields; never drop silently and never also send a duplicate vendorFeatures bag.

audioUsage.description: How referenceAudios are used. Distinct from generateAudio.

generateAudio.description: Whether the package should request generated audio in the output when supported.

steps.description: Example closed-set scalar. Packages declare only the scalars they support.

NamedResolutionExample.description: Illustrative alternative size representation: named resolution tier id. A real operation that chooses this representation omits width/height and resolutionValue.

resolution.description: Submit the package-provided tier id, never the UI label text.

MegapixelResolutionExample.description: Illustrative alternative size representation: megapixels. A real operation that chooses this representation omits width/height and named resolution.
